name: Cartographer
text: Surveyors, guides and map-thieves who walk into the fog so the town does not have to. A Cartographer's real loot is the map: every expedition they survive pushes the fog back around the town.

features.name: Field Notes
features.text: Expeditions with a Cartographer reveal one extra region of terrain when they report back, and their reports are never wrong about what they saw.

features.name: Pathfinder
features.text: The party travels a third faster through terrain the town has already mapped and never gets lost in it.

features.name: Dead Reckoning
features.text: Once per expedition, the Cartographer can lead the party out of a lost fight back to the last safe camp, ending the encounter.

features.name: Survey Stakes
features.text: Leaves a waystone at a site; the town can post bounties there without sending a scout first.

features.name: Read the Land
features.text: Before a party commits to a site, the Cartographer names its most dangerous encounter in the report.

features.name: Master Chart
features.text: While the Cartographer lives in town, mapped regions stay revealed between expeditions for an extra season.

rt.townPerk: Maps fog: each return reveals terrain around visited sites.

name: Hedge Witch
text: Village herbalists, midwives and curse-breakers. They brew in the alchemist's shop between adventures and can turn a bad harvest or a plague caravan around.

features.name: Kitchen Alchemy
features.text: Brews one common potion from the town grimoire each day she spends in town, for free.

features.name: Hedge Magic
features.text: Casts druid spells from the SRD list, preferring healing and warding.

features.name: Poultice
features.text: Wounded heroes resting in a house she visits recover twice as fast.

features.name: Plague Ward
features.text: Halves the spread of disease in the district where she lives.

features.name: Curse-Breaker
features.text: Can lift curses from relics and heroes; the town may charge for it as a service.

features.name: The Green Recipe
features.text: Discovers one new grimoire recipe each season without a recipe-map minigame.

rt.townPerk: Free potions, faster healing, disease control.

name: Reliquarian
text: Relic-hunters licensed by temples and collectors. They open the tombs nobody else will and know which relic fragments are worth enchanting and which ones whisper.

features.name: Appraise
features.text: Knows the true value of loot; the party never sells a relic for less than it is worth.

features.name: Warded Hands
features.text: Immune to the first curse or trap each expedition triggers.

features.name: Fragment Sense
features.text: Expeditions with a Reliquarian bring back one extra relic fragment from ruins and tombs.

features.name: Seal the Vault
features.text: Can seal a cleared tomb so nothing returns to it for a season.

features.name: Binding Rite
features.text: Can bind a dangerous artifact so the town can store it without it corrupting a councillor.

features.name: Living Archive
features.text: Each artifact in the town's vault grants one lore secret about the villain.

name: Warden
text: Sworn defenders of a town's walls and roads. Wardens rarely go adventuring: they patrol, train the militia and hold the gate when the warband comes.

features.name: Sworn to the Walls
features.text: Fights at full strength inside the walls even when outnumbered; the gate does not fall while a Warden stands in it.

features.name: Patrol
features.text: Walks a patrol route each day, lowering crime and spotting spies in the districts on it.

features.name: Drillmaster
features.text: Militia trained by a Warden fight one tier above their gear.

features.name: Hold the Line
features.text: Defenders next to a Warden take less damage from siege engines and brutes.

features.name: Murder Holes
features.text: Doubles the damage of walls, towers and chokepoints during a siege.

features.name: Last Stand
features.text: Once per siege, rallies every defender, ending fear and restoring a third of their health.

rt.townPerk: Patrols cut crime and catch spies; key in sieges.
